text.p: Reacting to investor concern, the leader of Mexico's main left-wing opposition pledged that his party would act sensibly and responsibly if it won a majority in congressional elections next month.

Polls show the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) is likely to win the Mexico City mayor's election by a huge majority on July 6. It is also likely to increase sharply its representation in the lower house of Congress.

PRD leader Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador told Reuters in an interview that the spectre of losing the lower house was alarming government ministers who have relied for the past 68 years on the Institutional Revolutionary Party's (PRI) congressional majority to pass all their legislation.
"They are spreading fear telling people that if the opposition wins they will lose what they have, there will be chaos and capital flight", Lopez Obrador said in the interview, conducted Thursday.

"Just before the 1994 presidential elections, a banker, Roberto Hernandez, said something similar. If the opposition wins, there will be capital flight and devaluation. This indeed happened -- except that it happened with Zedillo".
Weeks after taking office, Zedillo, whose campaign motto was "He Knows How to Do It", presided over a bungled peso devaluation which plunged the country into its worst recession since the 1930s.
Business leaders and bankers are now claiming that the PRD's current economic programme would lead to an economic crisis worse than that of 1994-95 if implemented.
Lopez Obrador dismissed such talk as scare-mongering.

"We want a majority in the (lower) chamber...to remove the sharpest edges of the economic programme," he said. "This would be within the same economic framework, without extremism...We don't want to have a majority in the lower house to destabilise the country".
The PRD leader also promised that his party would act responsibly in Congress.
"If we propose something in the lower house which would affect political stability, that will boomerang back against us. We have to act with a lot of sense. We are very conscious of that," he said.
Bankers' leader Antonio del Valle accused the PRD Wednesday of planning to stop paying Mexico's foreign debt and predicted its programme would cause economic chaos.
Lopez Obrador dismissed Del Valle's comments as propaganda, saying the banker was a "leading member of the PRI".
"I am sure he hasn't read the PRD programme because he says we propose, among other things, to stop paying the foreign debt or stop paying half of the debt," the PRD leader said.

"We don't contemplate that in the program. We don't plan either to cancel debt or (to have a) moratorium. We set out the possibility in the medium term of achieving a renegotiation of the debt to free up money which would allow us to stimulate industry and create jobs".
Lopez Obrador said the PRD also planned to reform the tax system to reduce sales taxes on general consumption and increase duties on luxury articles.

Mexico could free up substantial extra resources to fight poverty by eliminating corruption, he added. At least 20 percent of public investment was diverted by corruption "and I'm probably underestimating".
"Mexico's problem is not only financial or economic," Lopez Obrador concluded. "Mexico's problem is fundamentally political."
